subject: Dedicated capacity — throughput targets & $/1M token pricing follow-up
messages:
From: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@clearview.ai>
To: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
Cc: maya.singh <maya.singh@clearview.ai>
Date: Sun, 3 May 2027 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing & pricing (post-call notes)

Diego — thanks for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can move to an internal budget/ procurement review: 

- Traffic profile: ~peak batch jobs + interactive chat. Expected steady-state ~15M tokens/month with spikes up to ~40M in marketing-driven campaigns. 
- Target unit economics: our finance team wants to see base $/1M-token under $800 for committed capacity; <$600 would be ideal if achievable. 
- Preferred model mix: 70B-class chat model for customer-facing flows, smaller 13B for back-office. We expect ~70% of generation on 70B model. 
- Hardware preference: we asked your team about H100 vs A100 — company prefers H100 if pricing is reasonable, but open to A100 if it materially lowers costs. 
- Throughput targets: typical interactive SLA is 300–500 tokens/sec aggregate with concurrency for 10–20 reps; batch jobs can tolerate higher latency. 

Can you provide concrete reserved capacity SKUs with: GPU type, reserved lane quantity, estimated sustained tokens/sec, monthly committed cost, and implied $/1M-token? Also include any assumptions about caching, batching, or RLHF-impact that affect unit economics. 

If we can see a 2–3 SKU option (pilot, standard commit, high-commit) with clear $/1M math, I can take it to procurement next week. 

Thanks,
Alex

--
Alex Jenkins
Head of Product 
Clearview Analytics
alex.jenkins@clearview.ai
+1 415-555-0113

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jenkins <alex.jenkins@clearview.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing & pricing (post-call notes)

Alex — great to align yesterday. Below is a concise post-call recap plus three reserved-capacity SKUs based on the target volumes and model mix you described. I attached a draft pricing sheet and our 70B H100 benchmark summary for reference.

Recap / assumptions (short):
- Workload: 70B-class chat = 70% of tokens; 13B for remaining 30%. We priced assuming quantized 70B serving (Q4/8 hybrid paths) and continuous prefix caching for common prompts.
- Steady-state: 15M tokens/month baseline; planning SKUs sized for 40M peak headroom.
- SLA/throughput target: interactive steady ~400 tokens/sec sustained across the pool; bursts to ~900 tokens/sec for short windows.
- Caching & batching: we assume prefix/KV caching reduces token generation by ~12–18% for customer flows; batching efficiency for batch jobs adds 8–15% cost savings.

Proposed reserved SKUs (monthly committed):

1) Pilot — "H100-1"
- Hardware: 1x H100 80GB reserved lane
- Sizing guidance: suited for evaluation/pilot traffic up to ~120 tokens/sec sustained (interactive), burst to ~350
- Estimated monthly throughput: ~8M tokens/month (sustained profile + bursts)
- Committed monthly price (example): $9,000 / month
- Implied $/1M tokens: ~$1,125 (before caching benefits)
- Notes: smallest entry; good for 30–60 day pilot.

2) Standard — "H100-2"
- Hardware: 2x H100 80GB reserved lanes (pooling + autoscale buffer)
- Sizing guidance: sustained ~280–420 tokens/sec aggregate (fits your 300–500 target under normal loads), burst to ~900 with autoscale/burst credits
- Estimated monthly throughput: ~35M tokens/month
- Committed monthly price (example): $18,500 / month
- Implied $/1M tokens: ~$529 (before caching)
- Notes: quantization and caching assumed; we can tighten unit economics if you commit to a 12-month term.

3) High-commit — "H100-4"
- Hardware: 4x H100 80GB reserved lanes (dedicated pool)
- Sizing guidance: sustained ~600–900 tokens/sec aggregate, burst up to ~2,000 for campaign windows
- Estimated monthly throughput: ~90M tokens/month
- Committed monthly price (example): $34,000 / month
- Implied $/1M tokens: ~$378 (before caching)
- Notes: best $/1M with larger commit and includes priority routing and extended burst buffer.

A100 alternatives (cost-lower, perf tradeoff):
- A100 80GB lanes can reduce committed price by ~18–25% depending on availability. However 70B-class throughput will drop; expect ~20–30% higher latency for comparable batch sizes. If price sensitivity is primary and latency can be relaxed for some traffic, we can provide an A100-2 SKU equivalent for a lower $/1M.

Next steps I propose: 
- I will generate a formal quote + 12-month and 36-month committed price breaks by EOD Wednesday.
- Marissa / Ben: can you validate the pricing bands and confirm if we can offer an additional pilot discount (10%) and a 30-day pilot contract?
- Alex: if the Standard SKU looks closest to your budget target, confirm preferred GPU (H100 vs A100) and we will produce a signed quote + mutual action plan doc.

Attachments: pricing_sheet_draft.xlsx, benchmarks_70B_h100.pdf, mutual_action_plan.docx

Thanks — happy to jump on a 20-min call with procurement if helpful.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
diego@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0189

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — throughput targets & $/1M token pricing follow-up

Diego — this is very helpful, thank you. A few clarifications: 

1) The Standard SKU math looks closest to our target. Can you re-run the Standard SKU with a 12-month commit and show the $/1M with and without caching? If we can get near $450–500 /1M with caching included, that will get finance comfortable. 
2) We prefer H100 if the $/1M is comparable — please include explicit A100 comparators for the Standard SKU. 
3) Pilot: we prefer a 45-day pilot instead of 30 if you can offer the 10% pilot discount you mentioned. 

Please include a short paragraph on expected model fidelity/quality tradeoffs with quantization profiles — our ML team needs to sign off on any ~Q4/8 paths.

If you can send an updated quote and an MPA (mutual action plan) with milestones (pilot start, pilot metrics, procurement signoff) by EOD Wednesday that would be perfect. We'll aim to have procurement ready to review on Friday.

—Alex

From: diego_fernandez <diego@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: INTERNAL: Clearview — pricing bands + approval for 12mo quote and extended pilot

Marissa / Ben — forwarding the thread from Alex (Clearview). Key asks: re-run Standard SKU on a 12-month commit, show $/1M with/without caching, produce A100 comparator, and extend pilot to 45 days with a 10% pilot discount. Alex indicated procurement review on Friday.

Summary numbers requested to validate:
- Standard (H100-2) baseline: $18,500/mo -> show 12mo rate and implied $/1M assuming 35M tokens/month baseline.
- Show caching impact (12% and 18% scenarios) and final $/1M in both cases.
- A100-2 comparator with equivalent throughput and a clear note on latency/fidelity delta.

Attachments included for your decks: pricing_sheet_draft.xlsx, benchmarks_70B_h100.pdf (perf runs and token/sec assumptions), mutual_action_plan.docx

Can we lock internal approval for these numbers and finalize the formal quote by close Wed? If we need finance/discount approval, advise and I will escalate to RevOps.

Thanks,
Diego
